new_reasoning.because: OpenClaw's maintainers treat prompt injection as out of scope unless it crosses an authorization boundary, so the expected default-flip is a policy blocker rather than one release away.
new_reasoning.given: No agent configuration resists prompt injection, so the defense has to move to the harness - the one clause this week's evidence hardened rather than weakened.
new_reasoning.so_that: A clean install of a named harness runs sandboxed and capability-gated with zero extra operator configuration.
new_reasoning.landing: A named coding-agent harness defaults to capability gating by Q4 2026 - Claude Code v2.1.212 now leads on that, with OpenClaw absent from the slate.
new_reasoning.plain_language: Coding robots should block their own risky actions by default; the one expected to move first has ruled the problem out of scope, while a rival shipped it.
